subject: Banking
title: Alexander Hamilton's National Bank
description: One-minute skill: Alexander Hamilton's National Bank.

hook.text: Alexander Hamilton created America's first national bank in 1791. Thomas Jefferson fought him every step of the way.

buildup.text: Hamilton wanted a strong central bank to manage debt and stabilize the new nation.

discovery.text: The First Bank of the United States held government deposits, issued currency, and made loans.

twist.text: Congress refused to renew its charter in 1811. America's fear of centralized power killed its own successful bank.

climax.text: Hamilton built what worked. Jefferson feared what it meant. America has debated central banking power ever since.

punchline.text: Hamilton built the bank. Jefferson killed the charter. The debate never ended.

quiz.question: Why did Congress let the First Bank of the US expire?

details.summary: Alexander Hamilton established the First Bank of the United States in 1791 to stabilize the new nation's chaotic finances, consolidate war debt, and create a unified currency system, laying the foundation for American economic power.
details.whyItMatters: Hamilton's bank was the prototype for central banking in America. The political battle over its creation between Hamilton and Jefferson defined a fundamental question: should government centralize financial power or leave it to the states?
takeaways: The First Bank of the United States was chartered for 20 years in 1791
Hamilton argued a national bank was necessary to manage war debt
Jefferson opposed it as unconstitutional concentration of federal power
keywords: First Bank of the United States

faq.question: Why did Hamilton want a national bank?
faq.answer: The new nation had massive war debts, multiple state currencies, and no unified financial system. Hamilton saw a national bank as essential to establishing credit, stabilizing currency, and funding government operations efficiently.

faq.question: Why did the First Bank's charter expire?
faq.answer: Anti-bank sentiment and states' rights opposition led Congress to not renew the charter in 1811. Without a central bank, the financial chaos during the War of 1812 eventually convinced Congress to create the Second Bank in 1816.
